All participants are required to initiate treatment with a medium potency TCS using a standardized regimen. It is recommended that participants use triamcinolone acetonide 0.1% cream, fluocinolone acetonide 0.025% cream, or clobetasone butyrate 0.05%.

All participants should apply moisturizers throughout the study. All types of moisturizers are permitted, but participants may not initiate treatment with prescription moisturizers. Participants may continue using stable doses of such moisturizers if initiated before the screening visit.

dosing_regimen.source_excerpt: protocolSection.armsInterventionsModule.interventions; protocol Sections 5.1 and 7.2: "Pharmaceutical form: Solution for injection in pre-filled syringe;" "Participants will receive matching placebo" "All participants are required to initiate treatment with a medium potency TCS using a standardized regimen." "All participants should apply moisturizers throughout the study." "Participants received matching placebo every 2 weeks (Q2W) or every 4 weeks (Q4W) during the 16-week double-blind treatment phase." "Matching placebo was administered concomitantly with topical corticosteroids (TCS), including doubling the amount of placebo on Day 1 to match the loading dose." "Participants received subcutaneous injections of 600 milligrams (mg) loading dose on Day 1, then 300 mg of Dupilumab every 4 weeks (Q4W) from Week 4 to Week 12." "Participants received subcutaneous injections of 100 milligrams (mg) or 200 mg of Dupilumab every 2 weeks (Q2W)." "For 100 mg Q2W treatment group, participants received a 200 mg loading dose on Day 1, then 100 mg Q2W from Week 2 to Week 14." "For 200 mg Q2W treatment group, participants received a 400 mg loading dose on Day 1, then 200 mg Q2W from Week 2 to Week 14." "Dupilumab 300 mg Q4W + TCS" "Dupilumab 100 mg or 200 mg Q2W + TCS" "NCT03345914" "R668-AD-1652" -- Dose rows report maintenance doses and frequency; the registry result descriptions state the 16-week double-blind period and specific loading/maintenance doses. The loading doses are 200 mg, 400 mg, and 600 mg on Day 1 for Q2W <30 kg, Q2W >=30 kg, and Q4W respectively. Placebo recipients were assigned to matching Q2W or Q4W regimens. Protocol Arm A/B/C describe dose groups, but arm_names are left empty because CT.gov Group labels are not crosswalked here.

Very-high-potency/superpotent TCS prohibited. Recommended clobetasone formulation is unspecified.

value.source_inconsistency: The protocol describes two paths after Week 16: participants entering the OLE have Week 16 as end of study, while those declining/failing OLE have 12-week follow-up with visits every 4 weeks from Week 20 to Week 28. Thus end_of_study_week and total_duration_weeks are not single values for the whole cohort. Screening is up to 9 weeks; TCS standardization is 2 weeks; the combined screening plus standardization may not exceed 77 days. During treatment clinic visits are weekly through Week 4 and then every 4 weeks through Week 16, with weekly telephone visits in between.

value.rationale: Rescue may start only after a pre-rescue IGA assessment and for IGA=4 or intolerable symptoms. Investigators are encouraged, if possible, to try topical rescue for at least 7 days before systemic rescue; this is not an absolute prerequisite. Topical rescue may continue study treatment.

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: Protocol Section 7.3 Rescue Treatment: "Rescue treatment for AD may be provided to patients during the study." "treatment only in patients who either have an IGA score = 4, or have intolerable symptoms." "adequately after at least 7 days of topical treatment." "Patients who receive systemic corticosteroids or systemic non-steroidal immunosuppressive" "medication during the study will be discontinued permanently from the study drug." "will be asked to complete the scheduled study visits and assessments whether or not they" "use mometasone furoate 0.1% ointment as high-potency steroid." "If" "possible, investigators are encouraged to consider rescue initially with topical treatment (eg," "high-potency TCS) and to escalate to systemic medications only for patients who do not respond" "Patients may continue study treatment if" "rescue consists of topical medications." "The use of very-high-potency or superpotent TCS is" "prohibited in this study, even as rescue treatment, as their use is not recommended in patients" "under 12 years of age." "Very-high-potency topical corticosteroids include:" " Betamethasone dipropionate augmented 0.05% ointment" " Clobetasol propionate 0.05% solution, foam, cream or ointment" " Diflorasone diacetate 0.05% ointment" " Halobetasol propionate 0.05% cream or ointment" "drugs (eg, cyclosporine, methotrexate, mycophenolate-mofetil, azathioprine, etc) as rescue" "All patients" "complete study treatment and whether or not they receive rescue treatment for AD." "Investigators" "should make every attempt to conduct efficacy and safety assessments (eg, disease severity" "scores, safety laboratory tests) immediately before administering any rescue treatment." "An" "unscheduled visit may be used for this purpose, if necessary." "For the purpose of efficacy" "analysis, patients who receive rescue treatment during the study will be considered treatment" "failures." "7.4." "Dose Modification and Study Drug Discontinuation Rules" "7.4.1." "Dose Modification" "Dose modification for an individual patient is not allowed." "Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc." "Page 48 of 109" -- Systemic rescue with corticosteroids or non-steroidal immunosuppressants requires permanent discontinuation of study drug. The at-least-7-day topical-before-systemic sequence is encouraged if possible, not mandatory. The protocol tells patients to complete scheduled visits after rescue.

published_results.source_excerpt: Clinical Studies 14.1, AD-1652 Table 21, Week 16 FAS efficacy results: "Figure 2 Pediatric Subjects 6 to 11 Years of Age with Atopic Dermatitis The efficacy and safety of DUPIXENT use concomitantly with TCS in pediatric subjects was evaluated in a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (AD-1652; NCT03345914) in 367 subjects 6 to 11 years of age, with AD defined by an IGA score of 4 (scale of 0 to 4), an EASI score ≥21 (scale of 0 to 72), and a minimum BSA involvement of ≥15%." "Eligible subjects enrolled into this trial had previous inadequate response to topical medication." "Enrollment was stratified by baseline weight (<30 kg; ≥30 kg)." "Subjects in the DUPIXENT Q4W + TCS group received an initial dose of 600 mg on Day 1, followed by 300 mg Q4W from Week 4 to Week 12, regardless of weight." "Subjects in the DUPIXENT Q2W + TCS group with baseline weight of <30 kg received an initial dose of 200 mg on Day 1, followed by 100 mg Q2W from Week 2 to Week 14, and subjects with baseline weight of ≥30 kg received an initial dose of 400 mg on Day 1, followed by 200 mg Q2W from Week 2 to Week 14." "The primary endpoint was the proportion of subjects with an IGA 0 (clear) or 1 (almost clear) at Week 16." "Table 21: Efficacy Results of DUPIXENT with Concomitant TCS in AD-1652 at Week 16 (FAS) Full Analysis Set (FAS) includes all subjects randomized." "in Pediatric Subjects 6 to 11 Years of Age with AD DUPIXENT 300 mg Q4W At Day 1, subjects received 600 mg of DUPIXENT." "+ TCS Placebo + TCS DUPIXENT 200 mg Q2W At Day 1, subjects received 200 mg (baseline weight <30 kg) or 400 mg (baseline weight ≥30 kg) of DUPIXENT." "+ TCS Placebo + TCS (N=61) (N=61) (N=59) (N=62) <30 kg <30 kg ≥30 kg ≥30 kg IGA 0 or 1 Responder was defined as a subject with an IGA 0 or 1 (" ", Subjects who received rescue treatment or with missing data were considered as non-responders." "30% 13% 39% 10% EASI-75 75% 28% 75% 26% EASI-90 46% 7% 36% 8% Peak Pruritus NRS (≥4-point improvement) 54% 12% 61% 13% A greater proportion of subjects randomized to DUPIXENT + TCS achieved an improvement in the Peak Pruritus NRS compared to placebo + TCS (defined as ≥4-point improvement at Week 16)." -- Direct trial mapping: label names AD-1652 (NCT03345914), matching this task NCT ID, and says 367 children ages 6-11. Table 21 is Week 16 FAS (all randomized); its four values map in displayed order to dupilumab Q4W <30 kg, placebo <30 kg, dupilumab Q2W ≥30 kg, placebo ≥30 kg per table headings. Registry arm IDs map OG001 to Q4W dupilumab, OG002 to Q2W dupilumab, and OG000 to placebo. Published percentages and denominators are printed directly in the label; response rates were not computed from participant counts, so responders remain null and rate_is_derived is false. The table class title distinguishes duplicated placebo rows by weight stratum.
